notes.content:

We want to start by expressing our heartfelt thanks to every single one of you for your amazing support, dedication, and enthusiasm. Your passion is what drives us to keep improving the game every day. A special thank you goes out to everyone who took part in the beta testing of this patch—your feedback has been absolutely invaluable.
Thanks to the interest in the beta version, we’re expanding our beta testing platform for future patches. If you’d like to be among the first to test upcoming updates, make sure to follow us on our Discord channel: —we’ll be sharing all testing opportunities and announcements there!

Iron-related crafting balance changes - Iron Parts, Metal Tools and Machines

Refined Jade - balance cost of crafting

Balance changes in extracting tools - hatchet and pickaxe damage in primitive and improved version are fixed

Added some missing requirements building materials in various structures (Nine-arch Bridge, Farm)

[hr][/hr]🛠️ Core Gameplay FixesWe’ve also made crucial improvements to game mechanics and addressed several bugs:
Fixed major bug which blocks village managment menu

Quest items are now not tradeable

Fixed some minor warehouse issues: travel point position change, build collision expansion to cover for travel point, delete old travel points

Fixed bugs in Heavenly Ladder Monument - Building Progress issue and missing materials in few ghosts

Fixed bug which occurs when saving while building Nine-arch Bridge (objectives “Destruct wooden scaffolds”)

Building progress should be shown after placing fundaments

Further fixes on save system and loading sequences

[hr][/hr]🧭 UI & UX ImprovementsWe’re continuing to enhance the user interface for a smoother, more intuitive experience:

fixed bug which blocks crafting station/menu when using keyshorts during crafting

fixed bug which change handcraft menu with crafting station menu

Add missing knowledge menu entry about Iron Bars

Requirment resources in journal should now properly count items from Players inventory and caravan

Fixed some of problems related with mouse cursor loses focus

Fixed repeatedly appearing “new unlock” pop-up

Only valid saves will be shown in load save menu

Add some optional navigation in various menus

Added version Number in Main Menu and in Pause Menu


[hr][/hr]🧾 ...And That’s Not All!

Collectible Foliage / plants

Mountain area - more bayleaf to find

Lotus are now visible with outline

Quests


Quest givers from later stage of the game wont have tooltip before Player could interact

The Locust Plague, The Bandit King's Challenge, The Emperor’s Lotus Garden - fixed broken objectives

Minor fixes in quests: The Decorative Arts, The Weaver Girl and the Cowherd, Silk Road Merchant

Add some missing intrest point markers

Fixed optional dialogue in Engineering II quest, which could crash the game

NPC


Fisherman should spawn in correct position (not underground)

Village workers can now grow dye plants

Dialogue


Fixed empty dialogue option which crashed game

Add missing dialogue voiceovers in Metalworking and The Negotiation quests

Audio


Water audio effects in River area should be less intense (mainly when building nine-arch bridge)

Added missing audio effects for some decorations - bells and gongs

Minor fixes: jun footsteps, windmill sound fix on river, added workshop ambiences on level river, npc sounds updates

notes.title: Patch 1.02 | Fixes, Balancing, and the Road Ahead
notes.content:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/27426664b136160da1cb0ec4353269fd162a88bc.png"]
Hello, Builders!


Since launch, we’ve been overwhelmed by your support, feedback, and bug reports - thank you for being so active and involved. It means the world to us.

We might be a small team, but we're listening closely and working hard to improve Chinese Frontiers with every patch. Today, we’re rolling out Update 1.02, which brings a wide range of bug fixes, quality-of-life changes, and balance tweaks across farming, gathering, crafting, and quest progression.

Let’s take a look at what’s new!


[previewyoutube="PK8Zmv98gho;full"][/previewyoutube]

Polished and Patched
This update addresses some of the more disruptive bugs we’ve seen reported. From syncing issues in cutscenes to rice field snapping, cave resource issues, and visual glitches - many of these problems should now be behind us.

We’ve also made fixes to desert foliage, collision issues, and a few quest blockers that were holding back progress. If you ran into a bug while farming or noticed missing textures in monuments - those should be sorted now.


Farming Reworked
We heard you loud and clear - plant growth was too fast and rewards too random. With Patch 1.02, crop growth times have been rebalanced for a more natural pace, and drop rates have been increased across the board. You’ll also start finding seeds more often when gathering plants – helping you plan ahead.


Village Life Improvements
Your villagers are smarter now, too! They’ll gather more per tool and prioritize the most caloric food when eating. We’ve also made some changes to how fishing rods are used in storage and adjusted how resources stack.


Quest and Journal 
Dozens of quests received updated objectives, fixed VO/texts, or adjusted NPC positions for better visibility. We’ve also added item reset options to several main quests in case important items were lost - helping prevent blockers in progression.


That’s not all - check out the full changelog: 
Bug Fixes:

Fixed a bug where crops would grow instantly if players clicked repeatedly while planting

Desert map foliage: plants are now correctly visible and harvestable

River cave: fixed issue preventing iron ore collection

Fixed missing textures in the Desert map's Outpost Monument

Fixed the model of Jun appearing in the Mountain area

Fixed an issue with saving/traveling after death that could corrupt the save file in some cases

Fixed snapping issues and collision bugs with rice fields

Cutscene audio, subtitles, and video should be synced

Improved performance on the Desert map

Settings Fixes:

Language setting now saves correctly between sessions

Scalability setting no longer reverts to LOW

All graphic settings should now save properly

Quest Fixes:

Objectives and text improvements for:

Seeds of Jiumenkou

A Dark Omen

Recipes of Jiumenkou

Desert Drought

Mei’s Sanctuary

The Coop Keeper

Master of the Mud

Pillar and Hay

Recipes of Badaling

Recipes of Jiayu

Quest changes:

The Old Workshop

Alchemist

Mastering of the Flame

Missing VO Fix:

Hands to the Task

Main Quest Items Reset:

Added option to reacquire lost items for progression in:

Engineering I & II

Carpentry II

Decorative Arts

Bricklaying II

Decorative Arts: fixed issue with lanterns blocking quest progress

The Humble Harvest: tutorial update

Mei’s animals should no longer despawn

Additions:

Knowledge Menu now shows snail entry

Added source information for Lamb and Fish in Knowledge Menu

Added HP regeneration when hunger and thirst are above 80%

Changes: Tool Durability

Primitive tools: 50 → 150

Improved stone tools: 150 → 350

Gathering:

Trees yield more wood: 5 → 15 units per log

Rocks: increased drop rate by 20%

Rocks respawn time reduced: 900 seconds

Limestone respawn time reduced: 100 seconds

Crafting Adjustments (Carpenter Station):

10 wood → 20 raw planks / raw beams / wedges

10 raw plank → 15 planed plank

10 raw beam → 15 planed beam

20 wedge → 20 brace

5 wood block → 20 grid

15 planed plank → 15 carved plank

15 planed beam → 15 custom beam

15 brace → 15 duogong

Farming Adjustments:

Growth times increased:

Most crops extended from ~2 min → ~4 min (some to 7–8 min)

Drop rates increased:

Most crops: 1–3 → 1–6 units

Rice: 1–4 → 1–6

Flax: 2–4 → 2–6

All harvestable plants can now yield 1–2 seeds

NPC & Village Management:

NPCs now gather more resources per tool

NPCs consume highest-calorie food first

Fishing rod durability increased: 5 → 25 fish per rod

UI / Mechanics:

Resources and materials now stack up to 500 units

Interiors:

Visual improvements to the Stonemason’s Sanctum interior
Looking Forward
And yes, we’re continuing work on even more quest-related improvements - from interest point clarity, to journal usability, and deeper tracking tools for what’s next.



This patch is just the beginning. We’re still hard at work on:


Additional save system improvements;

Quest polish and better onboarding for new players;

Further balance tweaks to food, cooking, farming, and NPC management;

And of course - even more bug fixes and quality updates based on your reports.

notes.title: DevLog #18 - Keeping the Fire Burning | Gathering in Chinese Frontiers
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/181527d459a81d6b36e795e101d3d6147abba505.png

Hello, Builders!

A growing monument needs more than ambition - it needs resources. In Chinese Frontiers, gathering is the foundation of your progress, survival, and prosperity. Surroundings are full of valuable materials - ready to be shaped into something greater.

And today, we’re diving into the heart of resource gathering: how it works, what you’ll find, and how it fuels your journey forward.

Get it started

Every structure begins with the basics. Wood, stone, and bamboo will be among the first resources you collect, and they’ll remain central throughout your entire adventure. 

Wood can be picked up from the ground or harvested by chopping shrubs and trees of various sizes. It’s used for building materials and tools. 

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀ ⠀  ⠀ ⠀ ⠀ ⠀ {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/ca78f39efce28561222fca35cdd3a37bec7ae5b3.gif

Bamboo, on the other hand, is gathered from tall, slender stalks and used primarily in scaffolding and lighter construction. It’s flexible, plentiful, and indispensable when laying down the foundations of your early village.

Stone and limestone are a builder’s best friends. Gather loose stones from the ground or break down small boulders to obtain usable chunks. For more serious needs, you’ll mine from larger rock formations and rich mineral deposits. Limestone, meanwhile, is ideal for fine-tuned construction and decorative work.

Dig and mine

Not all resources come from forests and hills. Clay and sand are just as vital, and you’ll dig for them in dedicated pits, often near rivers or building zones. Clay shapes your walls and molds. Sand helps form your foundations - literally.

Iron and jade represent a step forward in your development. Iron is mined from specialized nodes and, once smelted, becomes the backbone of advanced tools, machines, and structural supports. Jade, rare and beautiful, is used in your most refined decorative creations - statues, ornaments, and architectural highlights.

Let me cook! 

Out in the wilds, you’ll also find flax, rice, dye herbs, and edible plants. Some grow freely and can be gathered. Others can be cultivated from seed in your fields.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/a2e29096eb92ffd50e09b9454ff57890389ec184.gif

These plants support your village in more ways than one. They bring flavor to your dishes, variety to your diet, and color to your world.

And if you're after something different? Grab your rod and head to the nearest stream - fishing offers a quieter rhythm to gathering, and a unique food resource for your next meal.

Managing 

With all these materials flowing in, proper storage and usage become essential. That’s where warehouses, workshops, and production chains come into play.

You’ll need to decide how to use each material: components for tools, ingredients for recipes, or inputs for crafting. Some are renewable, others rare. Stockpiling is one option - but smart usage and planning will always reward you in the long run.

Built from the Ground Up

In Chinese Frontiers, gathering is something that keeps everything else going. From fueling your workshops to feeding your people - it makes growth possible and monuments rise.

So next time you swing your pickaxe or cast your line, remember - every resource brings you one step closer to something greater.

notes.title: DevLog #17 - Rise and Work | Daily Routines in Chinese Frontiers
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/e782f31d26240d827717c3b88962f82d9b68f1f2.png

Builders!

Another day begins in Chinese Frontiers, and while construction might be at the core of your experience, it’s far from the only thing on your to-do list. Life in your village is full of rhythm and variety - woven together by more than just bricks and blueprints.

There’s a whole world to engage with - gathering resources, farming, fishing, cooking, and crafting. These daily routines are what truly bring your world to life. And in Chinese Frontiers, every task counts.

More than just building

Building is important - but it’s just one part of the bigger picture. Your day might start deep in the forest, chopping bamboo or collecting edible plants. Maybe you’ll head into the mountains to mine for stone, iron, or jade. Or perhaps you’ll cast a line into a quiet stream and bring home a fresh catch.

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀ ⠀  ⠀ ⠀ ⠀ ⠀ {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/db3d1cce019c16e8288308d0550f9e209a54041f.gif

Exploration plays just as big a role. You’ll venture through winding caves, lush forests, valleys, and other remote corners of China. Each environment offers new sights, resources, and challenges. Whether it's a sunlit rice field or a fog-drenched mountainside, every area invites you to explore further.

And back home, there’s work to be done. You’ll tend to fields, care for pigs and chickens, and make sure everything keeps moving. Your crops - like rice and other regional plants - support not just your household, but the entire community.

Create, Cook, Decorate

Once your resources are gathered, it’s time to get creative. In your workshops, stone is shaped, tools are crafted, and iron is forged. Over in the kitchen, regional dishes are prepared - meals that do more than restore strength. They’re a part of life and a way to care for those around you.

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀ ⠀  ⠀ ⠀ ⠀ ⠀ {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/f1f11f525da88c09d0c87fbf5d979b948c678a91.gif

It’s because the village is yours to shape. Lanterns and statues, banners and bells, carved gates and sculpted figures - all can be placed, refined, and arranged to reflect your style. Decoration is more than beauty - it’s the identity! 

Work together, grow together

As your settlement expands, teamwork becomes essential. Assign workers to key tasks, plan infrastructure, and build a village that reflects your vision. Homes, roads, workshops, storage buildings - they all take shape through careful coordination.

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀ ⠀  ⠀ ⠀ ⠀ ⠀ {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/1432adfde56e77dbc1e38d6e145d710b1d6200f5.gif

And then there’s the Great Wall. Monumental in both size and meaning, it demands everything you’ve learned - planning, patience, and skill. It’s not just another building project. It’s your legacy, carved in stone.

Build Your Own Routine

So whether you’re decorating a lantern, harvesting rice, forging tools, or overseeing a towering wall section - it all starts with rising and working.

notes.title: DevLog #16 - Working with Purpose | Tools in Chinese Frontiers
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/7871c424d8caec76963d8fee6cb2bf934a64ee31.png

Builders!

It’s time to roll up your sleeves and get your hands dirty - today we’re talking about tools. Breaking rocks, raising towers, chopping wood… We’ve designed a tool system that’s practical, immersive, and that evolves with your progress and craftsmanship.

Tools with Purpose

Every construction begins with the perfect tool, right? But not all tools are created equal. As your village expands and your workshops become more advanced, so does the quality of your gear.

Each tool in the game comes in three distinct variations:

Primitive - crafted by hand with basic materials, ideal for just getting started.
Improved Stone - built in an upgraded stonemason’s workshop, offering a great balance of durability and efficiency.
Metal - forged in a metallurgical workshop, these are top-tier tools built for longevity and heavy use.

This layered system lets you scale your tool usage with your evolving infrastructure.

Made by Hand…

Let’s take a closer look at the essential tools that will accompany you from the very first swing. Each one has been designed to serve a specific role in construction, gathering, or farming - and they just feel great to use.

The hammer is your go-to building companion. You know, bamboo scaffolding, sturdy wooden frames, and reinforced metal supports… It’s the tool you’ll return to again and again. Expect to carry one at all times - it’s practically an extension of your arm.

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀ ⠀   ⠀  ⠀ {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/65d5c0d5bb3ea6db1bef49b28d93847b2e685b5d.gif

When the forest calls, the hatchet answers. Ideal for chopping wood and bamboo, it’s an indispensable tool for those moments when nature becomes your materials supplier.

Let’s not forget the shovel! Great for collecting sand and clay, but also a vital tool when it comes to shaping terrain and laying stable foundations. It blurs the line between excavation and construction in the best possible way.

Need to dig into stone or uncover valuable resources? The pickaxe is your best friend when it comes to mining! This tool delivers strength where it matters most - it’s a must-have when the terrain gets tough.

A story of ambition and legacy

At its heart, Chinese Frontiers is a journey of growth, perseverance, and discovery. You step into the shoes of a young man with a past shrouded in mystery, taken in by an aging builder named Jun. Pillars of your journey

Mastering the Craft - Your journey as a builder starts with simple projects but soon expands to grand undertakings. From constructing rural homes to Monuments of the Great Wall, every structure you build brings you closer to earning the Emperor’s recognition.

notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/af822dba76d8c6cff63a06f803973938bf87e334.png

Builders!

The holiday season is coming, and while the world outside is sparkling with festive cheer, life in Chinese Frontiers is all about addressing the essential needs. This time of year reminds us of what truly matters - caring for ourselves and those around us. 

With that in mind, we think this is a perfect opportunity to talk about survival - what you’ll need to keep going in the game and how to nurture the people who call your village home. Grab a cup of hot tea, wrap yourself in a cozy blanket, and let’s dive in!

The Builder’s Needs

As a builder in Chinese Frontiers, you’re at the center of everything. But to build something big, first, you need to take care of yourself. Your stamina will be your constant companion, powering every step, jump, and construction effort. While it gradually recovers, pushing too hard without a break could leave you winded.

Then there’s hunger and thirst - the most basic yet critical needs. A growling stomach or parched throat can quickly turn even the simplest task into a challenge. The good news? Cooking in Chinese Frontiers isn’t just practical - it’s satisfying. Every dish not only fills you up, but also provides other benefits: boosts statuses or temporarily stops them from depleting.

⠀⠀⠀    ⠀⠀⠀    ⠀⠀⠀  ⠀    ⠀⠀⠀    ⠀⠀⠀  {STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/eda1f07b266ca0272ab74d1fac63103d7c0ac9b7.gif

And let’s not forget about health! Whether you take a nasty tumble or face an unexpected hazard, maintaining good shape is vital for survival. Managing this aspect isn’t just about staying alive - it’s about thriving. 

Oh, and remember to keep your stats high to unlock bonuses that make your journey even more rewarding! Trust us, you won’t regret it!

The Heart of the Village

But survival isn’t just about you. Your village is a living, breathing community that relies on your leadership. Each villager has their own needs, and meeting them is key to creating a thriving settlement.

First up? Home. A roof over their heads is non-negotiable. Without a proper house, no villager will consider joining your ranks. Providing shelter is the first step in turning your settlement into a bustling hub, so take care of it!

Once your villagers have a place to call their own, it’s time to get to work. Building a Warehouse is essential for managing the logistics of your growing community. This central hub keeps everything organized, guaranteeing that food, tools, and materials are always on hand.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/d4cc3d0358d774e4adafe71a449f66a1fb11a622.jpg

Celebrate with us

As we celebrate this festive season, we’re reminded of how far we’ve come - and how exciting the road ahead looks. Don’t forget to follow us on social media and join our official Discord server for more behind-the-scenes updates, sneak peeks, and chances to share your thoughts with us.

notes.title: Chinese Frontiers: DevLog #7 - THE SOUNDTRACK
notes.content:
Hey Chinese Builders!

We're back with fresh DevLog updates, straight from the recording studio where we just wrapped up the soundtrack for Chinese Frontiers!

What Unusual Thing Connects Poland and China? 

We know that people in China value ethnic music and love Frederick Chopin, who was actually Polish! Since we couldn't exactly ask Chopin to compose the music for our game, we got Ignacy Zalewski, Dean of Composition at Fryderyk Chopin University in Warsaw, to help us out. It's almost like getting Chopin, right?

Ignacy composed, and incredible musicians recorded, and now, here it is (imagine guzheng intro), 
THE SOUNDTRACK FOR CHINESE FRONTIERS!

[previewyoutube=Loe7dzSm39Y;full][/previewyoutube]
Well, it’s still in progress, but you can hear some pieces featuring various ethnic instruments like Guzheng, Er-hu, Suka Biłgorajska, Drums and Flutes. Not all these instruments are Chinese, but they’re all ethnic – that counts, still good enough. Plus, in Poland where we’re developing the game, we don’t have easy access to all Chinese instruments, so we improvised. Luckily, Mingjie played the guzheng, and Ada played the Er-hu. Awesome! 😊

The custom soundtrack is made just for you, to immerse you in the ancient Chinese atmosphere while exploring your world in Chinese Frontiers. The soundtrack will guide you through serene landscapes and bustling construction sites of the Great Wall, evoking wonder and peace. This music is incredible! You'll feel the calm and relaxation. We’ll also give you access to the soundtrack separately so you can enjoy it anytime, not just while building the Great Wall!

Stay tuned!

Please note that the soundtrack is still in development, but we’re excited to give you a sneak peek! :) Check out these tracks you’ll be able to enjoy while exploring the Chinese rural settlement.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pnDlr83WA8I

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-2mQPldr8vo

The recordings took place last week at the prestigious Polish Radio studio. Each session was a journey, exploring the rich textures and emotive power of traditional Chinese music. To preserve sound clarity and simplify post-production, the musicians recorded their tracks in separated acoustics, ensuring that every note and nuance was captured with pristine detail.

[previewyoutube=uz1Nu8AtZ9w;full][/previewyoutube]
The man behind this incredible musical experience is Ignacy Zalewski, a renowned composer of classical, film, theater, and radio music, and a professor at the Fryderyk Chopin University of Music in Warsaw.  Wojciech Lubertowicz, a multi-instrumentalist and sound director, provided the rhythmic foundation with his skillful drumming, ensuring that every beat resonates with the spirit of medieval China.

notes.title: Chinese Frontiers – A Journey Without Borders
notes.content:
Hello, Chinese Frontiers Builders!

We are back! After a brief break from our devlogs and announcements, we are excited to share updates on the past few months and our future plans for Chinese Frontiers! 

Our team has been working tirelessly, and we are proud to announce that Chinese Frontiers will be released globally this year!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/96c3615d07968d88cd043c7848cbce59383ddedc.png

By launching directly to full release, we ensure that our community worldwide can enjoy the complete, fleshed-out experience from the start—no Early Access phase!

Development Recap

Since our initial announcement, Chinese Frontiers has evolved significantly through various stages of development.

Our journey began with a promising demo, where players built one of the Beacon Towers of the Great Wall of China. This demo captivated over 40,000 unique users. It was followed by the Chinese Frontiers Prologue (over 55,000 unique users, review rate Mostly Positive, 77% in date), which featured an extended tutorial in a sandbox level and the player’s production base — Village. Both, the demo and the Prologue, were extensively tested through Steam's playtest sessions. The most recent feedback was sought from the Playtest of a new level—the Desert Fort at Jiayu Pass.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/e0b4d5238be0e12fcbfae379affa6ad9fe8e0610.png

Feedback

Each of these phases was crucial in sculpting the game’s direction and mechanics, heavily informed by player interactions and the feedback we received through surveys, our Discord server, and Steam Discussions.

We took that feedback to heart. Some of you had the chance to witness the changes we have made based on your opinions. There is a significant difference between our demo and prologue versions that you can test yourselves. We have added story quests and narrative for better immersion. Those of you who played the Desert Fort playtest may have noticed the new and improved tutorial system. There were many adjustments to give you a better experience, and there are still plenty that will be introduced in the upcoming full release!

The insights gained from these sessions were invaluable. We refined gameplay mechanics, enhanced narrative elements, and optimised user interfaces to make exploring ancient China as immersive and engaging as possible.

We especially want to thank our Chinese players for their suggestions and comments. Being based in Poland, Europe, the warm words and constructive feedback about Chinese culture, art, and language have helped us make our game more authentic and atmospheric.

We are profoundly grateful for the enthusiasm and support from our community throughout the development process. Your active participation in our playtests and your detailed feedback have been fundamental in shaping the final product.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/85b041074ef6181fb01ee32d087978082b083e35.png

Conclusion

Originally, Chinese Frontiers was slated for an Early Access release in Q2 2024. However, based on your feedback, we've made the strategic decision to skip Early Access. As we aim for a release later this year, we have given ourselves more time to fully develop our game. This decision not only streamlines the release process but also ensures that we are able to provide you with a coherent and immersive experience, complete with rich storytelling, enhanced gameplay mechanics, and beautifully crafted environments that will transport players directly into the majestic world of ancient China.

Stay tuned for further updates, and don't forget to add Chinese Frontiers to your wishlist and follow our Steam page.

notes.title: Chinese Frontiers: DevLog #6
notes.content:
Hi, my name is Marcin, and I am the Art Director for Chinese Frontiers. You may remember me from our first devlog (Devlog #1). This time, I want to share a bit about the food and cooking mechanics in our upcoming game. In order to survive and create a thriving settlement in Chinese Frontiers you may take advantage of those mechanics.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/6bc624888958493fd4d7f493f790a03bd44a606e.png

Immersive world

Although the game primarily focuses on architecture, building, and all activities related to this process, we knew from the start that incorporating side mechanics would enhance the player's experience. After releasing the technical demo of our project, we searched for interesting gameplay and cultural touchpoints to create a game with a unique atmosphere.

Everyone knows the saying: the way to a heart is through the stomach.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/5acbd157a6836aa49ba361b73c3703b6b2da3aef.png

The food and cooking mechanic plays a significant role in the game's immersive world. From a gameplay perspective, it complements farming, fishing, and breeding mechanics and at the same time enhances hunger, thirst, and stamina mechanics with short-term buffs. Moreover, the variety of ingredients and dishes showcases the differences between regions of China that the player visits. Note: While some of the dishes in our game may not be historically accurate, we still believe it's enjoyable to cook regionally relevant courses.

Could you taste these differences? 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/b462e0062f0059bccf9887b38e8e412d155a93c9.png

Cook your dish!

Our cooking mechanic is a unique and intricate system that plays a crucial role in the daily life of the settlement. With 14 recipes and 27 ingredients, players can experiment with various combinations to fulfill their hunger and other needs. Each group of ingredients and dishes is typical for a different area of China, including desert, mountain, river, and village cuisines.

The system distinguishes between Common dishes and Governor-worthy dishes. Common dishes fulfill hunger and provide a slight boost to health, while Governor-worthy dishes fill up one additional parameter such as thirst or stamina. However, after eating a Governor-worthy dish, some parameters are frozen for a few minutes, adding a strategic layer to the game. 

The ultimate goal is to find and eat the Emperor-worthy dish, which fills up all parameters and freezes them for a brief period. This rare and valuable dish can provide a much-needed boost in a critical moment or save a player's life in a dangerous situation. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/23353223d8473c56eb09e5a17da50c331fb052fb.png

Our goal in creating Chinese Frontiers is to build an immersive and realistic world rooted in Chinese culture. The food and cooking mechanics are an essential for adding more spice and flavor into this world.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/662350dc246b90d747cb7667b1e18e32d6e9706f.png

Let us know in the comment which traditional Chinese dish would you like to prepare!

notes.title: Chinese Frontiers: DevLog #4
notes.content:
Greetings, fellow adventurers! 

Marcin (Commando) and Tomek here, excited to talk about our part in creating our upcoming game, "Chinese Frontiers." As game designers and programmers, it's our job to bring the game world to life and make it engaging for players.

In our previous devlogs, we showcased the game loop and the amazing 3D assets our talented crew has been creating. Today, we're here to talk about what we've been working on specifically - interactive assets, resource gathering, building, upgrading, crafting, and more!

Building and Crafting

One of the core mechanics we've been working hard on is the building system. We had to make sure that it is intuitive and fun to use. You'll be able to upgrade buildings to unlock new features, craft tools and building materials to build even more stuff.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/c0bd8a36eeed7eff8fa06d6e362de37d9d7d0323.png

Crafting was an especially interesting subject for us as we wanted to add something more immersive for a player to interact with. Some of the crafting stations require more in-game actions from the player, rather than just selecting a recipe from the list. My favorite one is crafting bricks, and I am curious which one you like the most. Should we expand more on those ideas and add more crafting like this?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/77f02e887a22e8dd12c6cd05ff86ba46d5ada374.png

The Monuments

Moving on, let's talk about the main goal of "Chinese Frontiers" - building the Great Wall of China. But before you can do that, you need to gather materials, process them, and build up your Village. When you are ready, you will embark on a mission to build monumental parts of the Great Wall of China! In your journey you will use various tools to create them, starting from the crane which will help you to pull up heavy building materials. From programming code to the visual aspect and ending on audio design, we've put a lot of effort into creating an immersive crane experience.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/35c3911eaafcf27d109e415bd82515f1cdccfc3f.png

One of the most significant challenges in building the Great Wall of China is the height of the wall. That's where the scaffolding comes in! We've added the scaffolding mechanic to help players build at higher places with ease. You'll be able to stack scaffoldings on top of each other, allowing you to reach new heights and build impressive structures. But be careful not to fall off while you're up there! 💀 We wanted to make sure that players could enjoy building at higher elevations without sacrificing the fun factor, and the scaffolding does just that.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/023a7a6b553291ec91e8c286d12a3414b84cd129.png

Caravan

Another interesting tool that will aid you is the Players Caravan. It will allow you to transport necessary materials crafted in your Village to the Great Wall of China. The Caravan is connected to all workshops you place so you won’t have to transport all of the crafted materials in your own hands. Whenever you travel to the Monuments building site, your Caravan will be waiting for you with your materials ready. Hopefully, nothing will go missing during your travels! 😉

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/fa6053f155bf429f59e613c07795a67c0f28dc18.png

Making multiple intertwined systems that will allow setting up a monument of such a massive scale and will be easy to use for us, developers, proved to be an interesting challenge.

Skill System

As the game continues, players will have the opportunity to improve their character's abilities through various skills. These skills can boost their carrying capacity, increase movement speed, enhance farming abilities, and more. As players progress through the game, they will have the chance to invest in different skills, which will allow them to complete tasks more efficiently and make the most out of their resources. The skill system will add a layer of depth and strategy to the gameplay, as players must carefully choose which skills to invest in based on their playstyle and priorities. We believe that the skill system will add another layer of depth to the gameplay and give players a sense of progression as they develop their character's abilities. 
We're excited to see how players will use their skills to overcome challenges in "Chinese Frontiers"!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/b9b70dab68d316511397bc052e0c6b1e17f05444.png

From Gatherer to Village Boss

As your Village grows, you'll need to assign work to your cohabitants. This feature will be introduced in the early access stage of the game as we are still working on it. We want to make sure that as the game progresses, you'll start to feel more like a manager and not just a simple farmer, as you oversee the production and technology of your village.

There's More!

And that's not all. There will be different levels in the game, each with its unique challenges. For example, cooking original Chinese dishes typical for each area will be a fun way to experience the different areas. 

We're excited to bring these mechanics to life and can't wait for you to experience them in "Chinese Frontiers"! 

Thank you for following our journey, and stay tuned for more updates!

notes.title: Chinese Frontiers: DevLog #3
notes.content:
Hello! My name is Iza, and I'm a 3D Graphic Designer for Chinese Frontiers. In today's devlog, you will learn a bit about the process of modelling the buildings (workshops) that you will soon be able to construct on your own in our upcoming game!

Research and sketching 

Like almost everyone on our team, I am an architect - and thanks to this, when designing buildings, I paid attention to historical accuracy with traditional Chinese constructions. Before the actual modeling, I spent a lot of time on research. I used old sketches, books and films to better understand the whole process. It was definitely a very interesting stage of my job. 😃

After the research, it was time for design. Work on each building started with a sketch of the functional plan - so that its final form would be derived from the function it is intended to serve. During that time I also made a lot of loose sketches, as a way of thinking about possible forms. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/f4ddeb214f911525c33811ffa9378fc0353ee581.png

2D to 3D transformation 

The next, and really important step, was gradual transition from 2D to 3D. I created a lot of simple block models for each buildings - different alternatives - so that, even in 3D, before the final modeling, the scale, proportion, and arrangement of each building could be better sensed.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/2e975cf94bf81bf90186a32d9d9ad80c9d6ebd2c.png

As a result, each of the buildings gained a blocky, simple form for further work. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/a7e32b1fc60d33873de44c2ab00f314a8b8cdd69.png

Traditional Chinese wooden constructions often utilize intricate wood joinery techniques, where wooden pieces are interconnected without the use of nails or screws. Instead, interlocking joints are carefully crafted to create stable and durable structures. In Chinese Frontiers, you’ll be able to construct five different workshops, each of them has a different structure, tailored to the scale of the object and the function it is intended to serve.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/da01e7ca1afe5359abc2e8830f14a657cd8b9a9a.png

Texturing

Final step was detailed modelling and texturing. Here is a comparison between the initial sketch version of the building and its final form:

notes.title: Chinese Frontiers: DevLog #2
notes.content:
Hello everyone, my name is Bartek, UI/UX Designer and Game Designer for Chinese Frontiers. If you have a little time I would like to show you all of the challenges and dangers awaiting you in the beautiful landscapes of ancient China. Are you brave enough? 

Okay, so you wake up one day surrounded by beautiful landscapes, as you breathe in crystal clear air. You see a small but inviting settlement in the distance. Smoke coming from many chimneys. You don’t know why but you feel a sense that you belong here! Is this your Village?

The first mechanic of the game is your Village ( HUB ). At the beginning you and your village have very little to start. You get the basic fundamental infrastructure - but it hints at a great potential of growth. However, before you start working you have to think about few things:

1. Survival

Living in simpler times wasn’t necessarily easier. You have to think ahead to survive. Food and Water are the most important elements. Fortunately for you, Chinese landscapes are filled with fauna & flora that can help you stay alive. Gather different kinds of plants, use a fishing rod made of bamboo to catch some fish, drink straight from the river - water is clear. Survival is key.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/d44b6200f3b34ba9250067097644fb1789f93c38.png

Being a gatherer is fun and all, but if I had to guess you are ambitious and would like to expand. Changing a small Village into a thriving city will require a lot of resources and work, but I have good news for you. Try:

2. Farming, Breeding, Cooking

Work smart, not hard. Why run around all the time when you get hungry or thirsty. Turn yourself into an experienced farmer. You just have to pick a place for your field, get a hoe and some seeds and you are good to go! Remember every plant you gather gets you seeds that can be planted, but some of them are harder to find than others. 

When it comes to breeding, in the Prologue, it's an experience that is a very stripped down version. However, we are currently working on a more advanced system where you will be able to take care of your animals. If you take good care of the farm you will be able to use animal products that you collect in multiple different ways (Food, Trade, Building materials etc.).

Combine these products in the kitchen to cook real local dishes from different Chinese regions. 

Fun fact: The more complex the dishes are, the bigger reward you get! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/1916bb93e92a8dad1433553b3a1a4a7f146891c5.png

When your stomach is finally full, you can focus on the bigger picture. Imagine yourself as not only a Craftsman but an experienced Builder and City Planer. The Village is your starting point - nothing is stopping you but your imagination. 

3. Planing, Building, Crafting

At the beginning when the game starts there isn’t a lot to work with. You have to create a Basic Infrastructure that will allow your settlement to grow. Use your surroundings to gather resources - cut down trees with a hatchet to get wood, craft a pickaxe and use it on mountain formations to get stone, look under your feet for clay and sand. Everything can be used. So look around every chance you get.

Fun fact: all gatherable resources can be highlighted! 

When you feel you have enough resources open the Building Menu and pick your first project. There are a number of different buildings - Carpenter, Brickyard, Stonemason ect. Find a place where you want to place it and begin the building process. Basic materials are enough at the start, but with time, you will have to transform them into more complex, sturdy materials to upgrade your Village. 

Fortunately, every building has crafting stations that will allow you to do exactly that. Some of them are simple, some require you to really work hard and get your hands dirty, for sure you will manage.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/b2d04eb0bd81e1aa3b68db366e99068cd71c79d3.png

Finally, you have basic infrastructure to produce different kinds of building materials. Everything starts to look promising. Village is growing and people are happy! Nevertheless you don’t want to stay in one place. Why would you? Adventure awaits!

4. Travel, Build, Get Rewarded

Open your Map to see all of the Monuments of the Great Wall of China that require your experienced help. Pack everything on your trusty Caravan, pick a place to go and start your next adventure. I promise you will not be disappointed.

Every time you finish one of the big projects, you will be rewarded. Not only with the highest honor and well deserved place in the history, but also with new technologies (that will allow you to expand your Village) and new locations (with new interesting, challenging tasks).

But if you need some rest from the big picture stuff, always remember to try the side quests that we prepared for you. It will pay off in the end!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/e25bea9b743877e0a9ed1fafd0fcc1a070c1c553.png

So, to summarize REMEMBER:

With preparation you can survive anything.

With better materials you get better buildings.

With better buildings your Village gets more advanced. 

With better Village you unlock new technologies and get more complex and fun challenges. (BUILDING MONUMENTS OF THE GREAT WALL OF CHINA)

Completing these challenges unlocks new technologies and materials. 

If you play your cards right, before you notice you will be a true LEGENDARY BUILDER

notes.title: Chinese Frontiers: DevLog #1
notes.content:
Hi my name is Marcin. I am the Art Director and Producer of Chinese Frontiers and I welcome all of you to the very first of our DevLogs!  

Chinese Frontiers is the stylized builder simulation game with survival elements. The story is set in Ming Dynasty’s inspired Chinese reality, when the Great Wall of China was built.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/00bcd2c05ff21e5a4050575990b2be5a27b1d651.jpg

The Great Wall 
The main goal of the game is to obtain material, transform it and then build the Great Wall of China. Moreover, all of the Great Wall mission’s are the actual Great Wall Landmarks!
  
In Early Access we are going to build:

👉 Jiankou Great Wall ‚Sky Stairs’
👉 Great General’s Building of the Jiayuguan Fort
👉 Jiumenkou ‚The Nine Arch’ Bridge 
👉 The Tower - the Great Wall ‚signage’

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/ed45f36aeb6bdedeee503fcc86b592829b542535.jpg

The playground
China is the land of picturesque landscapes and biomes, from Jiuyuguan Desert to the heights of Huanglouwa. We analyzed them, synthesized and put into the game. Feel the heat of the Desert, the strong current of the River on the Plainland and the steep slopes of the Mountains! 

Fun fact!: All of the game biomes are totally different to each other. You will experience that, for example, by cooking original Chinese Dishes typical for each area! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/98194ba9f3c9e71546f3212ad84cd1cf9b608a46.jpg

Your new Homeland - the Village
While playing and getting more experienced through the game, you will get noticed by the Emperor himself! He will notice your sacrifice and determination and will commission you the management of the Village - the production and technology hub.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/bc9731efdf1db69174c143371942629ddbaf03ac.jpg

Craft & Survive
You will start your Journey with nothing. To survive you will need to get familiar with the nature - there is a lot of plants and resources to use in Chinese Frontiers! 

Then you will need to learn how to Craft and Grow what you’ve gathered. Your Production pipeline covers the variety of the Workshops, where Building Materials, Tools, Machines and Decorative Items are being made. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40819211/59b35f05222f19f5e8f20c9e656e2b59b2d244c7.jpg

At one point, when your Village will get bigger and bigger you will feel more like steward - assigning for some of the work your co-habitants (this feature will be introduced in the EA).


The DevTeam - our story
(for those who love reading a lot 🤓)

We are a group of friends, and our friendship is based on passion to storytelling about historical architecture and building - and we decided to make the game! 

I’ve met Iza (3D Graphics Designer) & Bartek (Game Designer and UI/UX Designer) many years ago on the sketching course, where we were learning and after few years also teaching others how to paint and draw. Wojtek (Level Designer and Tech Artist) & Piotrek (CEO - so at the end 😉) I’ve got to know little time later on the Faculty of Architecture. That’s why Chinese Frontiers is mainly about building so far. 🙂 Marcin (Game Designer and Programmer) called 'Commando’ is my good friend from childhood. Tomek (Programmer) & Michał (Community Manager) I’ve met during the development of Chinese Frontiers, but like the rest of the Team, we’ve got to know long time before. 

I can’t tell You how honored and lucky we were, when Igor & Iza (Audio Designers) and Ignacy (Composer) joined the Chinese Frontiers game project. More than they’re professionalists in their disciplines, they also are Lecturer’s on the Chopin’s University of Music (Ignacy is the Head of the Composition and Theory Music Department). 

Moreover, we’re also working with really talented Artists remotely and worldwide, trying to make our best for you guys. 

Prepare for more info about Chinese Frontiers and regular DevLogs soon, everyone has his/her own interesting story. Let us know in the comment if you like to read more about it at the end of our next DevLogs. 🙂

Thank you for supporting us by being here!💙

Marcin
